Eline: Dutch and Flemish form of Eleonora or Helena, ultimately Greek, possibly 'torch' or 'bright one'. Also used as a variant of Aline.
Ariana: Latinised form of Greek Ariadne, 'most holy' or 'very pure'. Also used as an Italian and Spanish variant of Ariane.
Alexis: Greek, from alexein 'to defend, help'. Used for boys in French and Greek; in English also for girls.
Marwa: Arabic, from the name of a hill near the Kaaba in Mecca; the word refers to a smooth, hard flint-like stone.
Lila: Probably a short form of Delilah or Leila, or from Sanskrit lila 'divine play'. Also Persian and Arabic 'lilac' or 'night' uses.
Khadija: Arabic, usually explained as 'premature child'. Borne by the Prophet Muhammad's first wife, so widely used among Muslims.
Sohan: South Asian, from Sanskrit/Hindi, meaning 'handsome, charming' or 'sweet'. Also found as a Persian-influenced name.
Kato: Origin uncertain in Belgium; probably a short form of Katharina or Katrien, from Greek 'pure'. Also a Ugandan name for a twin.
Lise: Short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'. Used in French, Dutch and Scandinavian languages.
Hafsa: Arabic, from hafs, 'young lioness' or 'gathered, collected'. Name of a wife of the Prophet Muhammad.
Mina: Short form of names ending in -mina, such as Wilhelmina, from Germanic 'will' and 'helmet'. Also Persian 'blue enamel' and Japanese 'beautiful'.
Lilou: French diminutive blending Lili or Lilian with Louise or Lou. Probably a modern French pet name.
Roos: Dutch for 'rose', the flower, from Latin rosa. Also a short form of Rosalie or Rozemarijn.
Nelle: Short form of Eleanor, Helen or Danielle, or from Nel. Probably a French and Dutch pet form.
Harry: English pet form of Henry, from Germanic heim-rik 'home ruler'. Also a medieval form of Harold.
Ayaz: Turkic and Persian, meaning 'clear, cold, frosty night air'. Also the name of Sultan Mahmud's famous companion.
Yuna: Japanese, with meanings such as 'gentle, kind'. Also a Korean name and a modern variant of Yvonne in Europe.
Ana: Spanish, Portuguese and Slavic form of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, 'grace, favour'.
Rosa: Latin for 'rose', the flower. Also sometimes a short form of Rosalia or Rosamund.
Fil: Short form of Filip or Philippe, from Greek Philippos, 'friend of horses'.
Ishaq: Arabic form of Isaac, from Hebrew Yitzhak, 'he laughs'. A prophet in Islam.
Célia: French and Portuguese form of Celia, from Latin Caelia, a Roman family name linked to caelum 'heaven'.
Joséphine: French feminine of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, 'he will add'. Famous as Napoleon's first wife.
Odin: Norse, from Old Norse Óðinn, from óðr 'frenzy, inspiration'. Chief god of Norse mythology.
Elodie: French, from Late Latin Alodia, from Germanic alod 'property, estate'. Possibly linked to a saint Alodia.
Diana: Latin, Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon; probably from the root of dius 'divine, bright'.
Suzanne: French form of Susanna, from Hebrew Shoshannah, 'lily' or 'rose'.
Jannah: Arabic for 'paradise' or 'garden'. Widely used among Muslims for girls.
Ulysse: French form of Ulysses, the Latin form of Greek Odysseus, of uncertain meaning, perhaps 'wrathful' or 'trouble'.
Neyla: Variant of Arabic Nayla, 'one who attains' or 'successful'. Also a modern spelling of Neila.
Malia: Hawaiian form of Maria; also Polynesian. Ultimately from Hebrew Miriam, of uncertain meaning.
Jennah: Variant spelling of Arabic Jannah, 'paradise, garden'. Possibly also an English form of Jenna.
Wassim: Arabic, meaning 'handsome, graceful, of fine features'.
Sienna: From the Italian city of Siena, also a colour name, 'burnt sienna'. Modern English given name.
Cataleya: Modern name from the Cattleya orchid, named after English collector William Cattley. Popularised by film and media.
Liya: Variant of Leah or Lia, Hebrew 'weary', or Ethiopian and Russian forms. Probably a modern spelling variant.
Sasha: Russian pet form of Alexander or Alexandra, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Leonardo: Italian and Spanish, from Germanic leon-hard, 'lion' and 'brave, hardy'.
Ilyan: Probably a modern variant of Ilyan or Elian, linked to Elias or Julian. Origin uncertain.
Marcus: Latin, probably from Mars, the Roman god of war. A common Roman given name.
Aliyah: Arabic 'exalted, noble'; also Hebrew aliyah, 'ascent'. Variant of Aaliyah.
Flora: Latin, 'flower'; Roman goddess of spring and flowers.
Basil: Greek Basileios, from basileus 'king, royal'. Also the herb name, which comes from the same root.
Celeste: From Latin caelestis, 'heavenly'. Used in French, Italian and English.
Mon: Probably a short form of Simon, Raymond or Ramon, or a Dutch Limburg pet form. Origin uncertain.
Musa: Arabic form of Moses, from Egyptian 'child' or Hebrew 'drawn out'. Also a Swahili name.
Elio: Italian and Spanish, from Greek helios 'sun' or Latin Aelius. Also a short form of Elia.
Sami: Arabic, 'elevated, sublime'. Also a Finnish short form of Samuel.
Aylin: Turkish, from ay 'moon' and the suffix -lin; sometimes explained as 'moon halo'. Also a variant of Aylin from Welsh.
Lior: Hebrew, 'my light'. Used for both sexes in Israel.
Jana: Czech, Slovak, German and Dutch feminine of Jan, from Hebrew Yochanan, 'God is gracious'. Also an Arabic name.
Sophie: French form of Sophia, from Greek sophia, 'wisdom'.
Janne: Dutch and Scandinavian pet form of Johanna or Jan, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. In Finland a male name.
Mathys: Dutch and Flemish variant of Matthijs, Dutch form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Jerome: From Greek Hieronymos, 'sacred name'. Saint Jerome translated the Bible into Latin.
Céline: French, from Latin Caelina, derived from Caelius or caelum 'heaven'. Also linked to Saint Cecilia's name.
Ahmad: Arabic, 'most praised'. A name of the Prophet Muhammad.
Soan: Probably a modern French spelling of Sohan or Sean, a variant of John. Origin uncertain.
Ayan: Arabic, Somali and Indian origin with varying meanings, such as 'gift of God' or 'God's blessing'. Also Sanskrit 'path'.
Scott: English and Scottish, originally 'a Scot', from Latin Scottus, a person from Scotland or Gaelic Ireland.
Lucia: Latin, feminine of Lucius, from lux 'light'. Saint Lucy is a patron of light and sight.
Souleyman: West African and French spelling of Arabic Sulayman, from Hebrew Solomon, 'peace'.
Liana: Probably a short form of names such as Juliana, or from the French liane 'vine'. Also Armenian and Georgian uses.
Aaliyah: Arabic, 'exalted, sublime, highest'. Popularised by the singer Aaliyah.
Odiel: Flemish form of Odilo or Odile, from Germanic aud 'wealth'. Rare in modern use.
Giorgia: Italian feminine of Giorgio (George), from Greek georgos 'farmer'.
Leya: Variant spelling of Leah, Hebrew 'weary', or of Leia and Leila. Probably a modern variant.
Martha: Aramaic, 'lady, mistress'. Biblical sister of Lazarus and Mary.
Ava: Probably from Latin avis 'bird', or a form of Eve or Germanic Avila. Also Persian 'voice, sound'.
Laya: Variant of Leila or Layla, Arabic 'night'. In Sanskrit laya means 'rhythm, merging'.
Maud: English and French medieval form of Matilda, from Germanic maht 'might' and hild 'battle'.
Mattéo: French variant of Matteo, the Italian form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Idriss: French spelling of Arabic Idris, a prophet, possibly 'interpreter' or 'studious'.
Aras: Turkish and Persian, from the Aras river in the Caucasus. In Lithuanian also an Eagle-related name.
Lorenzo: Italian form of Laurentius, 'from Laurentum', a Latin town, associated with laurel.
Olivier: French form of Oliver, probably from Latin oliva 'olive' or Germanic Alfihar 'elf army'.
Norah: Variant of Nora, a short form of Honora or Eleanor, from Latin honor 'honour'. Also an Arabic 'light' name.
Aslan: Turkic, 'lion'. Also the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books.
Nouh: Arabic form of Noah, a prophet in Islam, from Hebrew 'rest, comfort'.
Lore: Dutch and German short form of Eleonore, Lorena or Laura. Probably from Greek, Latin or Germanic roots.
Yassine: Arabic Yasin, a name of the Prophet and of a chapter of the Quran; meaning uncertain, often seen as mystical letters.
Joshua: Hebrew Yehoshua, 'the Lord is salvation'. The biblical successor of Moses.
Suze: Dutch short form of Susanna, from Hebrew Shoshannah, 'lily'.
Malak: Arabic, 'angel'. Used for girls in the Arab world.
Mara: Hebrew, 'bitter', in the Bible. Also Slavic 'Mary' short form and a Latin or Sanskrit root in some cultures.
Fatoumata: West African French form of Arabic Fatima, 'one who abstains' or 'weaner'. Fatima was the Prophet's daughter.
Léandre: French form of Leander, from Greek leon 'lion' and aner 'man'.
Malo: Breton, from Saint Malo (Maclou), possibly Celtic maglos 'prince'.
Maé: Breton and French, probably from Maël, 'prince, chief'. Also used as a short form of Marie.
Freya: Old Norse Freyja, 'lady'. The Norse goddess of love and fertility.
Théodore: French form of Theodore, from Greek 'gift of God'.
Nayla: Arabic, 'one who attains, wins'. Also a variant of Neila.
Aiden: Anglicised Irish Aodhán, from Aodh 'fire', a Celtic fire god. Also spelled Aidan.
Henry: English form of Henri, from Germanic heim-rik, 'home ruler'.
Frances: Feminine of Francis, from Latin Franciscus, 'Frenchman' or 'free one'.
Esther: Persian or Hebrew, probably 'star'. Biblical queen of Persia.
Louay: Arabic Luay, a diminutive of lu'a, perhaps 'bull' or 'shield'. Also a form of Louis in Arabic-speaking regions.
Mehdi: Arabic, 'the guided one'. The Mahdi is a messianic figure in Islam.
Gabrielle: French feminine of Gabriel, from Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Aloïs: French and German variant of Aloys, a form of Aloysius, itself of uncertain origin, possibly from Louis.
Phil: Short form of Philip, Greek Philippos, 'friend of horses'.
Emilie: French and Dutch feminine of Emil, from Latin Aemilius, 'rival' or 'eager'.
Marion: French diminutive of Marie, from Hebrew Miriam. Once also used for men.
Matheo: Variant of Matteo, the Italian and Spanish form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Leah: Hebrew, possibly 'weary' or 'wild cow'. Biblical first wife of Jacob.
Eloise: French and English, from Old French Héloïse, possibly from Germanic hailwidis 'healthy, wide'. Origin uncertain.
Leyna: Probably a modern variant of Lena or Leyla. Also similar to Hebrew 'to lodge'.
Amaya: Basque, from the Basque place name Amaia, meaning 'end'. Also Japanese 'night rain'.
Aylan: Turkic, 'moon' or 'moonlight' from ay, or Kurdish and Turkic 'lunar glow'. Origin uncertain.
Lionel: French diminutive of Léon, from Latin leo, 'lion'.
Lili: Short form of Elisabeth, Liliane or Lily. Pet form used in French, German and Hungarian.
Gabriella: Italian feminine of Gabriel, from Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Ona: Lithuanian and Catalan form of Anna, from Hebrew 'grace'. Also a Native American name.
Ryan: Irish Ó Riain, probably from rian 'king' or 'little king'. Also a given name in many English-speaking countries.
Colin: Scottish and French diminutive of Nicolas or Col, from Greek Nikolaos 'victory of the people'. Also Gaelic 'young creature'.
Zélie: French, from Saint Azélie or Zélie, probably from Greek zelos 'zeal'.
Seppe: Flemish short form of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, 'he will add'.
Adrien: French form of Hadrianus, 'from Hadria', an Adriatic town.
Evan: Welsh form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'. Also Irish Éoghan, 'born of yew'.
Jacob: Hebrew Ya'akov, 'supplanter' or 'may God protect'. Biblical patriarch.
Juline: French diminutive feminine of Jules or Julie, from Latin Julius.
Lucile: French form of Lucilla, a diminutive of Lucia, from Latin lux 'light'.
Médard: French, from Germanic mathu 'strong' and hard 'brave'. Saint Médard is a patron of weather.
Adrian: From Latin Hadrianus, 'from Hadria', an Adriatic town. Name of several popes and a Roman emperor.
Luan: Possibly Albanian 'lion', or Welsh 'light'. Also a Portuguese form of Lou. Origin uncertain.
Valentine: From Latin Valentinus, from valens 'strong, healthy'. Associated with Saint Valentine.
Lana: Possibly a short form of Alana or Helena. Also Slavic 'doe'. Origin varies by culture.
Hanna: Variant of Hannah, from Hebrew 'grace, favour'. Common in Scandinavia, Dutch and German.
Jad: Arabic 'generous' or 'jade'; also a Hebrew 'hand'. Often used in Lebanon.
Isabella: Latinate form of Isabel, from Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Mone: Probably a Dutch short form of Simone or Monique. Possibly from Japanese or German pet forms. Origin uncertain.
Adem: Turkish and Bosnian form of Adam, from Hebrew 'earth, man'.
Isa: Short form of Isabel, or Arabic form of Jesus, from Hebrew Yeshua. Also Dutch pet name.
Kayden: Modern American coinage, likely from Kaden or Aiden, perhaps blending Cadan. Origin uncertain.
Pauline: French feminine of Paul, from Latin Paulus, 'small, humble'.
Ismail: Arabic form of Ishmael, Hebrew 'God hears'. Prophet in Islam.
Ilias: Greek form of Elijah, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Lilly: English variant of Lily, the flower, or a short form of Elizabeth. From Latin lilium.
Mustafa: Arabic, 'chosen, selected'. A title of the Prophet Muhammad.
Nell: English short form of Helen, Eleanor or Ellen. From Greek helene, 'torch' or 'bright'.
Ismaël: French form of Ishmael, Hebrew 'God hears'.
Gus: Short form of Augustus or Gustav, from Latin 'venerable' or Germanic 'staff of the Goths'.
Senne: Flemish, from the Senne river in Brussels. Also a Dutch pet form of Sven or Sander.
Siebe: Frisian and Dutch, from Germanic sigu 'victory' with a diminutive. Related to Sybrand.
Matei: Romanian form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Layane: Probably a modern variant of Lyanne or Arabic Layan, meaning 'softness'. Origin uncertain.
Apolline: French feminine of Apollo, the Greek sun and music god. Saint Apollonia.
Achiel: Flemish form of Achilles, Greek, possibly 'pain of the people'.
Ties: Dutch short form of Matthias or Matthijs, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Violette: French, 'violet', the flower, from Latin viola.
Kenan: Turkish and Arabic, from Canaan; also Hebrew 'acquire'. Also a Welsh and Cornish name, 'little hunter'.
Ela: Turkish 'hazel-eyed', or a short form of Ella, Eleonora or Elisabeth. Also Hebrew 'oak, terebinth'.
Naya: Arabic 'to be near' or a Greek form of Naia. Also Sanskrit 'new' and 'leader'.
Sidra: Arabic, referring to the lote tree in paradise. Also Latin 'starry'.
Lyo: Probably a modern short form of Lyonel or Leon, from Latin leo 'lion'. Origin uncertain.
Lex: Short form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'. Also Latin lex, 'law'.
Lilia: Latin lilia, 'lilies'. Also a Slavic and Russian form of Lily.
Hana: Japanese 'flower'; also Arabic 'bliss' and a Czech and Slavic form of Hannah.
Mare: Short form of Maria or Marie. Also a Dutch and Frisian pet form.
Malya: Probably a variant of Mali or Malia. Also Arabic 'full', a modern spelling. Origin uncertain.
Aron: Variant of Aaron, Hebrew, possibly 'exalted' or 'mountain'. Also Scandinavian use.
Aisha: Arabic, 'alive, living'. Name of the Prophet Muhammad's wife.
Zeyd: Turkish form of Arabic Zayd, 'growth, abundance'.
Tristan: Celtic, from Drustan, from Pictish drest 'tumult'; later associated with French triste 'sad'. Hero of medieval legend.
Amy: English form of French Aimée, 'beloved', from Latin amata.
Rik: Dutch short form of Hendrik or Frederik, from Germanic rik 'ruler, powerful'.
Judith: Hebrew Yehudit, 'woman of Judea' or 'praised'. Biblical heroine.
Roman: From Latin Romanus, 'of Rome'. Common in Slavic countries and France.
Romeo: Italian, from Romeus, 'pilgrim to Rome'. Known from Shakespeare's tragedy.
Philippa: Feminine of Philip, from Greek 'friend of horses'.
Éléonore: French form of Eleanor, probably from Provençal Aliénor, possibly 'the other Aenor'.
Tessa: Short form of Theresa, or from Greek 'harvest'. Also a variant of Tess.
Célestine: French, feminine of Célestin, from Latin caelestis 'heavenly'.
Valentino: Italian form of Valentine, from Latin valens, 'strong, healthy'.
Elya: Probably a variant of Elia or Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'. Also a modern variant of Elia.
Salma: Arabic, 'safe, peaceful'; related to salam. Also a diminutive in Arabic and Spanish contexts.
Dario: Italian and Spanish form of Darius, from Persian 'holder of the good'.
Meryem: Turkish and Arabic form of Mary, from Hebrew Miriam, of uncertain meaning.
Uma: Sanskrit, 'tranquility' or 'light'. A name of the Hindu goddess Parvati.
Febe: Dutch form of Phoebe, from Greek 'bright, radiant'. Biblical figure.
Melissa: Greek, 'honey bee'. In mythology a nymph who nursed Zeus.
Louna: Probably a French blend of Louise and Luna, or from Lou and Anna. A modern coinage.
Jude: English form of Judas, from Hebrew Yehudah, 'praised'. Also a New Testament apostle.
Alexandra: Feminine of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Tess: Short form of Theresa or Tessa, possibly from Greek 'harvest'. Also Hardy's novel heroine.
Alixe: French variant of Alice or Alix, from Germanic Adalheidis, 'noble kind'.
Cécile: French form of Cecilia, from Latin Caecilius, perhaps 'blind' or 'dim-sighted'. Saint Cecilia is patron of music.
